sources.entry: Dockit - An application that can dock any window to the edge of the screen.

summary.one_liner: Dockit is a macOS window manager that docks windows to the left or right screen edge and shows them on hover.
summary.what_it_does: Dockit moves a window to the left or right edge of the screen with a keyboard shortcut. A docked window collapses to a narrow strip at the edge and expands when the pointer hovers over it, then collapses again when the pointer leaves. The README lists configurable settings such as exposed width and trigger area. It also offers a shortcut to undock a window, optional launch at login, and notifications. Setup requires granting macOS accessibility permission and restarting the app. The README is in Chinese and English-language headings are mixed in; no build or install commands are given.
use_cases: dock a window to the side of the screen
free up screen space while keeping a window handy
preview a window by hovering at the screen edge
quickly snap windows left or right on a Mac
keep a chat or music window tucked to the edge
how_to_run: Grant accessibility permission when prompted and restart the app
Press ⌘ + ⇧ + ← to dock the window left
Press ⌘ + ⇧ + → to dock the window right
stack: Swift (implied by macOS app; not stated)
notable: Hover to expand and leave to collapse a docked window at the screen edge
Configurable exposed width and trigger area
Customizable keyboard shortcuts for dock and undock
Credits Peninsula as a reference for window-specific implementation
caveats: Requires macOS accessibility permission and a restart after granting it
Only left and right edge docking is described
No install or build instructions beyond downloading the app
